AcknowledgementDetail.description:
One trusted consumer's claim about one aggregate, as a reader sees it.

``reason_code`` is from a closed vocabulary and carries no quantity, party or document
identity: a Catalog reader learns what to fix, not what Billing holds.
AcknowledgementDetail.title: AcknowledgementDetail

ActivityDefaultsInput.description:
A typed audited action, not a bare PATCH of pointer columns.

All four pointers are required, and `null` is a real value meaning *no default
configured* — resolution then reaches the built-in Main (§3). Requiring them stops an
omitted field from clearing a default the caller never mentioned.

Changing a default moves no stock and touches no quantity: it changes which location a
later operation resolves to, and only for operations that location is allowed to do.
ActivityDefaultsInput.title: ActivityDefaultsInput

AdvancedDefinitionCreate.description: Exact, bounded native definition command; SKU zero is the default slot.
AdvancedDefinitionCreate.title: AdvancedDefinitionCreate

AdvancedDraftContent.description: Transport state only; submission uses a separate strict native command.
AdvancedDraftContent.title: AdvancedDraftContent

BinCreate.description: A subdivision of one location. The location is part of the bin's identity.
BinCreate.title: BinCreate

BinUpdate.description: Label only. A bin cannot move to another location — that is a different bin.
BinUpdate.title: BinUpdate

BomDraftUpdate.description: Full reviewed aggregate replacement, including both complete child collections.
BomDraftUpdate.title: BomDraftUpdate

CompanyDraftInput.description: The owner is bound from the authorised company, never selected by the caller.
CompanyDraftInput.title: CompanyDraftInput

ConfigurationBootstrap.description: No input: the built-in location set is derived, never chosen by the caller.
ConfigurationBootstrap.title: ConfigurationBootstrap

ConfigurationControl.description: Closed native editor hints; authority still comes from FieldMetadata.
ConfigurationControl.title: ConfigurationControl

ConfigurationOptionItem.description: A protected native parent for opening the selected record's existing page.
ConfigurationOptionItem.title: ConfigurationOptionItem

CustomerPricingChain.description: One step of the audit chain returned by :func:`resolve`.
CustomerPricingChain.title: CustomerPricingChain

CustomerPricingEffective.description: The effective buyer-level read for a quote or invoice price lookup.
CustomerPricingEffective.title: CustomerPricingEffective

activation_available.description: Service support only; use activation preview for SKU eligibility.
activation_available.title: Activation Available

expected_default_item_version.description: Required when replacing default SKU attributes or declaring variant axes.
expected_default_item_version.title: Expected Default Item Version

gst_rate_default.description: Use dated company tax rates; undated suggestions are not authoritative.
gst_rate_default.title: Gst Rate Default

ImpactReviewDetail.description: Report metadata; the reviewed request body itself stays internal.
ImpactReviewDetail.title: ImpactReviewDetail

ItemReplenishmentPolicyInput.description: The product's whole set of bands. A scope left out is retired, never left stale.
ItemReplenishmentPolicyInput.title: ItemReplenishmentPolicyInput

ItemReplenishmentPolicyView.description: The product's reviewed bands. No on-hand quantity appears here: Catalog owns none.
ItemReplenishmentPolicyView.title: ItemReplenishmentPolicyView

ItemWarehousePolicyInput.description:
The product's whole location policy: the mode, the membership and the defaults.

Every activity default must also appear in ``locations``. A default pointing at a
location the product does not explicitly permit would be a permission asserted in one
column and denied in another, and it is what lets a location deactivation check its
dependencies with two indexed lookups instead of trusting a scan
(docs/catalog-warehouses.md §3, §5).
ItemWarehousePolicyInput.title: ItemWarehousePolicyInput

ItemWarehousePolicyView.description:
The product's stored policy, or the baseline that its absence means.

``is_configured`` is the honest distinction: ``false`` with ``ALLOW_ALL_ACTIVE`` says
"no row, so the location's own policy decides", never "somebody chose this".
ItemWarehousePolicyView.title: ItemWarehousePolicyView

LocationPermissionDetail.description:
One membership row through the caller's read policy.

Everything but the identity is optional and unset when a field policy denies reading it:
a read deny holds in projections, not only in forms (docs/field-permissions.md §6). An
entry whose ``warehouse_id`` is denied is omitted from the view entirely — its flags
would still disclose that the product is stocked somewhere the reader may not see.
LocationPermissionDetail.title: LocationPermissionDetail

LocationPermissionInput.description:
One location this product may be kept at, and the operations allowed there.

The flags are a narrowing of the location's own reviewed policy, never an addition to
it: a flag the location does not allow is refused rather than trimmed, so the stored row
means what the reviewer ticked.
LocationPermissionInput.title: LocationPermissionInput

OperationFlagsInput.description:
The eight typed permissions, all required.

Every flag is mandatory on purpose. A publish states the whole policy, so an omitted
flag cannot quietly keep — or quietly drop — the value it replaces, and the reviewer
approving the change sees all eight together (docs/catalog-warehouses.md §2).

There is no validity window here. The window is server-assigned at publish: these are
live controls resolved at operation time, and a caller-supplied start would be a
backdated permission change (§5).
OperationFlagsInput.title: OperationFlagsInput

OperationPolicyInput.description: The publish body: the flags, plus the expectations the preview handed back.
OperationPolicyInput.title: OperationPolicyInput

OperationPolicyPreview.description:
A dry run. Writes nothing, allocates nothing, and is not a reservation.

`expected_generation` and `expected_source_version` are what a publish must echo back;
if anything changed in between, the publish is refused rather than applied to a picture
the reviewer never saw.
OperationPolicyPreview.title: OperationPolicyPreview

OperationPolicyRevisionDetail.description:
One published revision. `effective_to` is set when a successor supersedes it.

Everything but the identity and the delivery state is optional and unset when a field
policy denies reading it: a read deny holds in projections, not only in forms
(docs/field-permissions.md §6).
OperationPolicyRevisionDetail.title: OperationPolicyRevisionDetail

OperationPolicyView.description:
What a location may do now, and what it was allowed to do before.

History is returned rather than summarized: a reader auditing a movement needs the
revision that was in force then, not today's flags.
OperationPolicyView.title: OperationPolicyView

PolicyReleaseInput.description:
Publish the company's stock-location policy as one numbered, dated release.

There is no manifest in the body. A caller that could state which locations a release
covers could publish a release that omits the one location it changed, and a consumer
reading it would enforce a policy the company never approved. Catalog builds the manifest
from its own reviewed rows and records the digest.

``expected_generation`` and ``expected_source_version`` come from the configuration read,
as they do for a defaults change: the release describes the company the reviewer looked at,
or it is refused.
PolicyReleaseInput.title: PolicyReleaseInput

PrimaryGroupInput.description:
One location's dated primary group.

``group_id`` may be ``null``, which closes the current membership and opens nothing:
"no group" is the absence of an open interval, never a row pointing at nothing. A
membership change grants and revokes no access to the location either way (§3).
PrimaryGroupInput.title: PrimaryGroupInput

ReleaseCommit.description: Publishes against exactly one review: a synchronous preview or a background report.
ReleaseCommit.title: ReleaseCommit

ReleaseDetail.description:
One release in full, with the acknowledgements that speak about it.

Everything but the identity and the delivery state is optional and unset when a field
policy denies reading it: a read deny holds in projections, not only in forms
(docs/field-permissions.md §6).
ReleaseDetail.title: ReleaseDetail

ReleaseListItem.description:
A release in the history list. Lean by design (docs/api-conventions.md).

``delivery_state`` is computed from the acknowledgements, never stored: Catalog can say
what it published, and only a consumer can say what is enforced.
ReleaseListItem.title: ReleaseListItem

ReleaseView.description:
The release in force, and the ones before it.

History is returned rather than summarized, for the same reason an operation policy's is:
a reader investigating what a consumer enforced last week needs the release that was in
force then, not today's.
ReleaseView.title: ReleaseView

ReplenishmentScopeDetail.description: One band through the caller's read policy. Quantities stay exact on the wire.
ReplenishmentScopeDetail.title: ReplenishmentScopeDetail

ReplenishmentScopeInput.description:
One reviewed band: at a named location, or for the product as a whole.

``warehouse_id`` is ``null`` for the product-wide band. Exactly one such band may exist
per product — the stored scope key carries a sentinel rather than ``NULL`` so that is a
unique constraint rather than a convention.
ReplenishmentScopeInput.title: ReplenishmentScopeInput

UnitListItem.description: Denied fields are omitted, never replaced with fabricated values.
UnitListItem.title: UnitListItem

WarehouseConfigurationDetail.description:
The company's location configuration, and the expectations a defaults change echoes.

`source_version` is the live Identity checkpoint, as it is on every other Catalog read:
a defaults change is refused unless it echoes this one back, so the read a reviewer
made and the write they submit describe the same company.
WarehouseConfigurationDetail.title: WarehouseConfigurationDetail

WarehouseGroupCreate.description:
A group and the interval its parent link opens.

``valid_from`` is required and dated from the start: the hierarchy answers "who did
this group report to on that date", and a create with no opening interval would leave
a group whose history begins nowhere.
WarehouseGroupCreate.title: WarehouseGroupCreate

WarehouseGroupReparent.description: Appends a future interval; it never rewrites the one in force.
WarehouseGroupReparent.title: WarehouseGroupReparent

WarehouseGroupUpdate.description: Identity only. The parent link moves through the reviewed reparent action.
WarehouseGroupUpdate.title: WarehouseGroupUpdate

WarehouseUpdate.description:
Identity and location facts. `kind` and `is_system` are not editable here.

A store that became a godown would silently change which operations a document may
perform against stock already recorded under it; that is a new location, not an edit.
WarehouseUpdate.title: WarehouseUpdate

catalog__schemas__configuration__DraftIn.title: DraftInput

Publish the company's stock-location policy as one numbered, dated release.

The manifest is Catalog's, not the caller's: the body carries the date, the reason and the
expectations the reviewer previewed, and nothing that could narrow what the release covers.

A typed reviewed action, not a PATCH of pointer columns: it changes where later
operations resolve to, so it needs `warehouse.publish` like a policy revision does.
